∫ (eˣ (1 + x)) / cos²(eˣ · x) dx =

Options:
A. -cot(eˣ) + c, where c is a constant of integration.
B. tan(x · eˣ) + c, where c is a constant of integration.
C. tan(eˣ) + c, where c is a constant of integration.

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Evaluate the indefinite integral ∫ (eˣ (1 + x)) / cos²(x eˣ) dx.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Substitute t = x eˣ. Then dt = (x eˣ + eˣ) dx = eˣ (1 + x) dx, which matches the numerator exactly.

key_concepts: Integration by substitution: t = x eˣ
Product rule derivative: d/dx(x eˣ) = eˣ(1 + x)
Standard integral: ∫ sec²t dt = tan t + c

key_formulas.substitution: t = x eˣ  ⇒  dt = eˣ(1 + x) dx
key_formulas.reduced_integral: ∫ 1 / cos²t dt = ∫ sec²t dt = tan t + c

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Substitute t = x eˣ, convert the integral into ∫ sec²t dt, integrate to tan t + c, and replace t with x eˣ.
logical_steps: Step 1: Let t = x eˣ ⇒ dt = eˣ(1 + x) dx
Step 2: Rewrite integral: I = ∫ 1/cos²t dt = ∫ sec²t dt
Step 3: Integrate: ∫ sec²t dt = tan t + c
Step 4: Substitute back t = x eˣ ⇒ I = tan(x eˣ) + c

step_1_substitute.dt: d/dx(x eˣ) dx = (1·eˣ + x·eˣ) dx = eˣ(1 + x) dx

phase_5_verify_answer.answer: B. tan(x · eˣ) + c, where c is a constant of integration.
